Devine",{"abbrev":393,"shortDisplay":393,"shortName":394,"globalSportId":220,"globalSportNameSlug":395,"globalSportGender":162,"id":396,"title":111},"2025-08-11T07:46:38.223","/sports/womens-soccer/roster/ireland-devine/16454",[4933,4962,4988],{"bio":4934,"twitter":21,"image":4935,"images":15,"displayFields":4940,"sport":4944,"latestCoachBioId":4945,"latestSupportBioId":15,"latestBioId":4945,"id":4945,"title":4946,"firstName":4947,"lastName":4948,"email":4949,"phone":21,"url":15,"staffId":4950,"socialMediaR":4951,"custom1":21,"custom2":21,"custom3":21,"custom4":21},"\u003Cp>Matt Micros enters his eighth season at the helm in 2025 with a 44-58-17 overall record and a 30-25-11 record in conference play. He is the third head coach in SHU's history.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn 2024, Micros led the Pioneers to their fifth consecutive playoff appearance in its first season in the MAAC. In five years in the NEC, the Pioneers reached the playoffs four times, reaching three semifinals with a championship game appearance in 2022. That game ended in a draw before FDU advanced to the NCAA tournament on penalty kicks. Overall, Micros has coached 9 players to all conference honors with an NEC Rookie of the Year nod for Michelle Clarkin in 2019. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHe posted his most successful season in 2022 with an 11-5-5 overall mark, including a non-conference road win over 2021 NCAA Sweet 16 program St. John’s from the Big East. Against the NEC, Micros led Sacred Heart to a third-place regular season finish with a 5-1-3 record. Victories over LIU and Merrimack landed the program in the conference championship game for only the third time in program history. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe 2024 season was one that saw the Pioneers overcome five season ending injuries and an 0-8-2 start, to stun eventual conference champion and cross town rival, Fairfield 2-1, as part of a four game unbeaten streak that landed the Pios back in the playoffs. SHU was the only MAAC team and one of only three teams to beat the Stags all season. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to arriving at SHU, Micros spent nine seasons as the head coach at Post University. Under his tutelage, the Eagles made six playoff appearances, reached three ECAC Tournament semifinals and won the ECAC in 2015. Micros was named the CACC Coach of the Year, leading the Eagles to the program's best record, 12-6-1, and the CACC Championship Game in 2014. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn addition to his collegiate coaching, Micros is the co-founder of the Connecticut Football Club where he oversees the ECNL girls program. He has coached four top 20 nationally ranked teams, and totaled 11 Connecticut State Cup Championships. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe development of players that can excel at the next level has been paramount in the growth of CFC under Micros' leadership. In the last decade alone, 127 CFC players have signed to play at Division I schools including: Boston College, Clemson, Indiana, North Carolina, Notre Dame, Northwestern, Penn, Penn State, and West Virginia. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMicros also served as the head coach of the Connecticut Olympic Development Program from 1997-2004, leading the team to a National Finals appearance in 2003. During that time, he coached numerous elite players, including Alyssa Naeher, the long time starting goalkeeper for the US Women's National Team. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nMicros graduated from the University of Notre Dame with a B.A. in American Studies. He earned an M.S. in Television, Radio & Film from Syracuse University's Newhouse School of Communications in 1990 and attended SHU's Graduate School of Education in 1995-96. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nA native of Pittsford, N.Y., Micros resides in Milford, Connecticut with his wife Katy and son Petrucelli was named the department's first female Deputy Athletics Director in 2021 and has assumed the designation of Senior Woman Administrator (SWA).   The purpose of the SWA designation is to promote meaningful representation of women in the leadership and management of an institution’s intercollegiate athletics program.  Through this role she will continue to provide leadership to men’s and women’s sports and issues. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Petrucelli oversees academic services and student development departments as well as NCAA and Title IX compliance\u003Cem>.\u003C/em>  She also has sport oversight of women's basketball, field hockey, swimming & diving, women’s wrestling as well as men's and women's' golf.  \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Petrucelli elevated the student-athlete experience at Sacred Heart University in her prior duties as Senior Associate Athletics Director for Student-Athlete Support Services.  Petrucelli has been instrumental in addressing the needs of SHU student-athletes on and off the field. She worked to provide priority class registration for in-season student-athletes and worked in partnership with university stakeholders to review and implement a streamlined academic standards policy for all students.  She played a pivotal role in reinvigorating the Faculty Athletic Mentor (FAM) Program to increase opportunities for student-athletes and faculty to connect and learn from each other. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Petrucelli introduced the \"Playbook for Success,\" a program aimed at setting up first-year student-athletes in their transition to college. She followed that with the creation of the “Jumpstart Your Semester Program” as well as the “Life After College” event. \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>She also saw a need to address student-athlete mental health by supporting the student led initiative, Heart-to-Heart a mental health awareness campaign. That led to a collaboration with the university counseling center and the dean of students to designate an embedded mental health counselor within the athletics department.     \u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Petrucelli serves on the Northeast Conference (NEC) DEI Administrative Committee and helped advise student-athletes in the creation of, Every Heart is Sacred, a student-led diversity, equity, and inclusion initiative.  She is a member of SHU’s WGSS (women’s gender sexuality studies) faculty/staff network.  Petrucelli is a member of the President's Athletic Advisory Committee (PAAC) and is the chairperson for the athletic department's Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging Committee.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>A graduate of American International College, Petrucelli joined SHU in 2011 as the Assistant Director of Placement for the College of Arts and Sciences within the Center for Career & Professional Development Office. Less than two years later she was promoted to director and provided counseling to SHU students in identifying majors and career paths that align with the student's goals, interests, and values.  She moved to athletics in 2014, as director for student-athlete support services, advancing to Associate AD in 2016, and Senior Associate AD in 2019. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nShe resides in West Haven, Conn., with her spouse,
